nodes.label: Audit de préparation à la production
Persisted Order State Machine (P0-1)
nodes.rationale: Kraken order execution and local persistence are not atomic; a crash, exception, or retried request after a real Kraken fill can leave a live order unrecorded locally. Requires a persisted state machine (PENDING/SUBMITTED/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED/FAILED/RECONCILE_REQUIRED) with a client-generated idempotency id created before the external call, plus reconciliation against Kraken for ambiguous states.

nodes.label: Kraken Private POST Auto-Retry Risk (P0-2)
nodes.rationale: urllib3.Retry allows POST in allowed_methods, so non-idempotent Kraken calls like AddOrder/CancelOrder can be silently replayed after a 429/5xx or connection failure, turning an ambiguous order state into real financial risk. Requires disabling blind retries on non-idempotent commands, monotonic cross-process nonces, and using a client order id (userref) to look up/reconcile before retrying.

nodes.label: Concurrent TP/SL Closure Risk (P0-3)
nodes.rationale: The TP/SL close path has no CLOSING state, distributed lock, or atomic claim; two watcher instances or a manual click during a watcher cycle can sell the same position twice. select_for_update() alone is insufficient if the lock is held across the network call. Requires a single active watcher instance and an atomic OPEN->CLOSING claim before the external sell call.

nodes.label: Global Authorization Model (P1)
nodes.rationale: All business views use login_required, but models have no owner and querysets use objects.all(); any authenticated account can view, edit, delete all trades/API keys and trigger a LIVE order. Only acceptable if the instance is explicitly single-user; a multi-user instance needs an owner FK, per-queryset filtering, and object permissions.
